title: Plan Export V1 (one handoff material rendered from one stored plan revision)
$comment: DL-KB-11. GET /api/projects/{id}/assistance-plans/{aplan}/export?format=markdown|txt|json|storyboard_csv answers this envelope. `body` is the exported material itself -- the bytes the designer keeps -- and everything else is what makes those bytes traceable: which revision they came from (`revision`, `plan_content_sha256`), the pinned dependency snapshot the plan recorded (`reference_snapshot`, copied from the stored document rather than re-resolved, so an export freezes what the plan claimed instead of restating today's objects), the emitter contract version (`emitter_version`), and the not-executed statement. Three of these are constants on purpose: `sent`, `executed` and `external_verified` are `const false`, because this repository has no outbound transport and no dispatch, so the only honest answer is a value a flag-flip cannot move -- turning any of them true requires a contract change here, not a code path elsewhere. `states` repeats the plan's own four states exactly as the readback computed them, with `externally_verified` pinned false again: exporting reads, it does not change. The `allOf` block ties `format` to the `content_type` and the filename extension a reader will actually get, so an answer that calls itself a 分镜 CSV and hands out a text/plain -- or names a .md file for a JSON body -- is refused by the contract and not merely by care; the shape a page can confuse is a mismatched pair, not a missing field. No schema here claims an export was delivered, and no field could: there is no such field.

allOf.$comment: format <-> content_type <-> extension, in all four pairs. A markdown body served as text/csv, or a .csv filename around a JSON document, is the mismatch a reader cannot detect from the text alone.
The 分镜 CSV is the only material with a byte-order mark, because it is the only one a spreadsheet opens directly; a CSV body without the BOM is the shape that shows 镜头说明 as mojibake in Excel.
